title.narrative: 1.3: 3 Local Workshops held in collaboration with Associate LGAs

description.narrative: 1.3: 3 Local Workshops held in collaboration with Associate LGAs for 120 stakeholders (40 per State) to dialogue on research findings and the mainstreaming of digital solutions in local government and rural development plans;

comment.narrative: 2 Local Workshops has been held so far with FUNAAB in Ogun State 13092023 14092023 and UAES in OwerriUmuagwo 18102023 19102023. Over 80 participants have been recorded at both Workshops from across the stake holding beneficiary groups including 6 LGA Government Commissioners of State for Digital Economy Agriculture and Environment State Cooperative Associations Traditional Rulers Private Sector Entrepreneurs and local Farmers. The EU Delegation has participated in the opening sessions of both Workshops to sensitize participants on the EU and Nigerian Government Green Deal and Digitalization Policies. The Survey Report and Best Practice have been shared and validated by the participants for recommendations.

3 Local Workshops were hosted to dialogue on research findings and mainstreaming of digital solutions in local government and rural development plans 3 Local validation Workshops were held in collaboration with Local Government Authorities at FUNAABAbeokuta 130920231492023 UAESOwerri 1810202319102023 and ALHIKMAHIllorin 07112023 08112023. The aim of the Workshops was to present the findings of the fieldsurvey in each State to local stakeholders share experience with other stakeholders and Partners and to validate the research reports. Key stakeholders participating in each Workshop includes State Officials from Agriculture Rural Development Commission Of Youth And Sports Commission of Environment Commission of Water Resources Rural Development Commission of Labour and Productivity Commission of Women and Social Development and Commissions for Digital Economy and Information. Others include cooperative unions farmers associations and Trade Unions amongst Civil Society Groups. Amongst the Private sector local agribusinesses and ICT Companies were invited including Finance Companies. Key recommendations from the Workshop include accessibility of technology to farmers and entrepreneurs development of new organic products for the market improved access to financing for farmers new financial products and digital solutions that make it easier for them to manage their own businesses and the role of financial institutions and agribusinesses. In total over 200 participants stakeholders and target groups participated in the local workshops both virtual and physically. It also provided opportunities for teaching staff in the 3 Partner Universities to visit each University promoting mobility and networking and to share best practices on research and development on digitalization in the agriculture sector.

Key Officials from the following Ministries participated in the Workshop. They include Ministry of Agriculture Rural Development Ministry of Environment Ministry of labour and Productivity Ministry of Women and Social Development Local Authorities. The role of women and gender in the leadership of agricultural cooperatives green farming and promotion of agrivalue chains was discussed.
